what_it_does: Numerical programs running on modern hardware — such as AI accelerators or processor units that handle many numbers at once — must balance two competing goals: getting accurate answers and running fast. Traditional compilers (programs that translate human-written code into machine instructions) focus only on speed for a given chip, while tools designed for numerical accuracy ignore what the target hardware can actually do. Chassis is a new compiler that jointly reasons about both accuracy and speed, exploring the trade-offs between them while respecting the specific instructions and capabilities of the target chip. For each numerical expression, it finds the implementation that delivers the best accuracy for the speed budget the hardware allows.
